doc.title: Folding a Paper: A Small Synthetic Study

sentences: We study how readers move between a paper's own words and short summaries of it.
Readers who could fold the text found the main claims faster than readers of the plain text.
We describe the reader and its limits.
Researchers read many papers each week [1, 2].
Most of that reading is skimming for the main claim (Lee et al., 2021).
Skimming saves time but misses how a claim is argued.
Summaries written by language models are short.
They do not show which of the author's sentences they rest on.
No reader we know links each summary line back to the text.
Each level keeps the words that the next level needs.
A reader can open any paragraph in place to see all of it.
The folds are stored beside the paper on this computer.
Each paragraph is folded into five levels, from a topic to the full text.
A word keeps its place across levels when it appears in both, scored by s = n / N. The PDF beside the text is matched by runs of three words.
